composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# A repeated create carrying an already-seen Idempotency-Key replays the originally
# created owner (200) rather than creating a duplicate. First seen (or no key): proceed
# to build. This runs first so the replay short-circuits before the duplicate check. It
# only reads an in-memory token store and branches, so it needs no transaction.
checkIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckIdempotencyKey
  outputs:
    proceed: build
    replay: replayLoad

# Replay branch: load and respond with the remembered owner (200), mirroring GET. A read,
# so readonly-transaction; reuses the shared RespondWithOwner responder.
replayLoad:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.LoadReplayedOwner
  govern: [ readonly-transaction ]
  next: replayRespond
replayRespond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwner
  govern: [ readonly-transaction ]

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: validatePostcode

# Validate the postcode (when present) against the city's region before any
# persistence work, so an out-of-range postcode is a 400.
validatePostcode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidatePostcode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: normalizeEmail

normalizeEmail:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerEmail
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: normalizeTelephone

normalizeTelephone:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerTelephone
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectDuplicateIdentity

# Hard duplicate detection (409): rejects an owner whose identityKey (SHA-256 over normalized
# telephone, lower-cased email and soundex(lastName)) matches an existing, non-deleted owner's.
# Runs after the email-domain blocklist and telephone normalization so the key is comparable.
rejectDuplicateIdentity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectDuplicateIdentity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: normalizeAddress

normalizeAddress:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerAddress
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectFutureRegistrationDate

# Reject a supplied registrationDate later than the server date (400), before the
# weekend-roll normalization so the check is on the supplied date.
rejectFutureRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectFutureRegistrationDate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: normalizeRegistrationDate

normalizeRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerRegistrationDate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

# Store the deterministic householdId (hash of last name + postcode) on the owner, for
# OwnerIdentity and the DTO. The duplicate check and household-size count below derive the
# household themselves, so they do not read this stored value.
assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectCityAtCapacity

rejectCityAtCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectCityAtCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectOverDailyLimit

rejectOverDailyLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectOverDailyLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: countHouseholdMembers

countHouseholdMembers:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CountHouseholdMembers
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCustomerCode

assignCustomerCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: countNamesakes

countNamesakes:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CountOwnerNamesakes
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: flagBulkSignup

flagBulkSignup:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.FlagBulkSignup
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignMembershipLevel

assignMembershipLevel:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignMembershipLevel
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: capMembershipLevel

# Cap the derived level to at most one above the current maximum membershipLevel among
# the owner's existing household members. No existing household member => no cap.
capMembershipLevel:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CapMembershipLevel
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: flagPossibleDuplicate

# Soft duplicate signal: shares an existing owner's lastName and postcode with a different
# telephone. Flags, never rejects; skipped for a declared household member (sharesHousehold).
flagPossibleDuplicate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.FlagPossibleDuplicate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: recordIdempotency

# Remember this owner under the request's Idempotency-Key (when present) so a repeat
# create replays it. After save so the owner has its id; no-op when no key was supplied.
recordIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RecordIdempotencyKey
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

audit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AuditOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]
=====REJECT EXAMPLE=====
package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner;

import net.officefloor.plugin.variable.Val;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.Owner;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.repository.OwnerRepository;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.escalation.CityAtCapacityException;

/**
 * Rejects creating an owner when the owner's city already contains 50 or more existing
 * owners. Cities are compared case-insensitively on their trimmed value. Runs before
 * {@link SaveOwner}, so the owner being created is not counted. A city at (or over)
 * capacity escalates as a 409 via {@link CityAtCapacityException}.
 */
public class RejectCityAtCapacity {

    private static final int CITY_CAPACITY = 50;

    public void service(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository ownerRepository)
            throws CityAtCapacityException {
        String city = owner.getCity() == null ? "" : owner.getCity().trim();
        long count = ownerRepository.findAll().stream()
                .filter(existing -> existing.getCity() != null
                        && city.equalsIgnoreCase(existing.getCity().trim()))
                .count();
        if (count >= CITY_CAPACITY) {
            throw new CityAtCapacityException(
                    "City '" + owner.getCity() + "' already contains " + CITY_CAPACITY
                            + " or more owners");
        }
    }
}
=====PROBLEMDETAILS=====
package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.escalation;

import java.net.URI;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.List;

import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.dto.ValidationMessageDto;

/**
 * Builds {@link ProblemDetail} bodies with the fields common to every escalation handler
 * (title = exception simple name, timestamp, empty schemaValidationErrors placeholder).
 */
final class ProblemDetails {

    private ProblemDetails() {
    }

    static ProblemDetail build(Exception ex, HttpStatus status, String detail) {
        ProblemDetail problemDetail = ProblemDetail.forStatus(status);
        problemDetail.setType(URI.create("about:blank"));
        problemDetail.setTitle(ex.getClass().getSimpleName());
        problemDetail.setDetail(detail);
        problemDetail.setProperty("timestamp", Instant.now());
        problemDetail.setProperty("schemaValidationErrors", List.<ValidationMessageDto>of());
        return problemDetail;
    }
}
=====CITYHANDLER=====
package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.escalation;

import net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter;
import net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;

public class CityAtCapacityExceptionHandler {

    public void handle(@Parameter CityAtCapacityException ex,
            ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail>> response) {
        ProblemDetail detail = ProblemDetails.build(ex, HttpStatus.CONFLICT, ex.getMessage());
        response.send(ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.CONFLICT).body(detail));
    }
}

VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The new pieces mostly land cleanly on the codebase's established patterns: `RejectDuplicateIdentity` mirrors `RejectCityAtCapacity` (same `service(@Val Owner, OwnerRepository)` shape, same `findAll` + skip-null-id + skip-same-id + skip-deleted loop, same checked-exception-escalates-409 convention), the exception/handler pair and its escalation YAML match the existing families exactly, `DuplicateOwnerExceptionHandler` reuses `ProblemDetails.build` like every sibling handler, and the YAML wiring slots `rejectDuplicateIdentity` in at the right point with a correct comment. Splitting `normalizedTelephone`/`lowerEmail` out as named package-private helpers on `OwnerIdentity` is a genuine readability win, and the stale `normalizedTelephone` copy in `FlagPossibleDuplicate` was correctly removed. So the additive shape is good — two structural issues keep it from LGTM.

1. **Duplicated SHA-256→hex routine (`OwnerIdentity.identityKey` vs `HouseholdKey.householdId`).** This diff introduces a second, near-verbatim copy of the hash-and-hex-encode block that already lives in `HouseholdKey.householdId()`:
   - `MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256").digest(... getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8))`
   - the `StringBuilder` + `append(String.format("%02x", b))` loop
   - the `catch (NoSuchAlgorithmException) → throw new IllegalStateException("SHA-256 not available", ex)`

   The only difference is full-digest vs first-6-bytes. This is exactly the kind of duplication this codebase explicitly designs against — `OwnerTelephones` and `HouseholdKey` are each documented as a "single source of truth … so the two can never drift." Extract the hex-SHA-256 step into one shared helper (e.g. a small `Hashing.sha256Hex(String)` / `Hashing.sha256HexPrefix(String, int)`), and have both `identityKey` and `householdId` call it. A maintainer here would not expect two independent copies of the digest routine.

2. **Soundex algorithm placement — `OwnerIdentity` is accreting a general string algorithm.** `OwnerIdentity` is documented narrowly as "Single source of truth for an owner's identityKey," but now also hosts a ~45-line general-purpose American Soundex implementation (`soundex` + `charCode`), which `FlagPossibleDuplicate` reaches into purely for last-name similarity matching — a household/name-matching concern, not identity-key construction. The codebase's own idiom is to give a reusable, self-contained rule its own focused helper (`OwnerTelephones` for phone normalization, `HouseholdKey` for the household definition). Soundex fits that mold and would be more natural as its own helper (e.g. `Soundex`, or folded into the household/name-key helper), with both `OwnerIdentity` and `FlagPossibleDuplicate` depending on it directly. As written, `OwnerIdentity` is becoming a catch-all for "all string-normalization used anywhere near identity," and `FlagPossibleDuplicate`'s dependency on it for name matching reads as borrowing rather than a genuine identity-key use.

Neither is a correctness concern — both are about putting the logic in the right unit and not duplicating the hashing step the codebase already single-sources.
